title: 04. OOP: Properties (@property, @setter, @deleter)
summary: Imagine you have a thermostat on your wall. You can read the temperature, you can set a new temperature (but only between 16°C–30°C — it won't let you set 500°C!), and you can reset/delete the custom setting.

quiz.explanation: 5-Year Experience Answer: "@property is a decorator that creates a managed attribute — when you access obj.salary, Python invisibly calls the getter method; when you assign obj.salary = 50000, it calls the setter.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a read-only property and a regular attribute?
options: Answer: "Yes — obj.static_method() works and is equivalent to ClassName.static_method().
5-Year Experience Answer: > "Instantiation is the process of creating an object from a class.
Answer: "Grouping — it keeps related functionality inside the class namespace.
5-Year Experience Answer: > "A regular attribute can be freely set and overwritten: obj.total = 999 works.
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Experience Answer: "A regular attribute can be freely set and overwritten: obj.total = 999 works. A read-only property (only @property, no @setter) raises AttributeError when you try to assign: obj.total = 999 → AttributeError: can't set attribute.

5-Year Experience Answer: > "self is a reference to the current instance of the class.

quiz.explanation: 5-Year Experience Answer: "If you define only @property (getter), the attribute becomes read-only. Attempting to set it raises AttributeError: can't set attribute. However, there's a subtle gotcha: if the underlying private attribute (__name) doesn't exist yet, even reading will fail.

quiz.question: What is a computed property? How is it different from a stored attribute?
options: 5-Year Experience Answer: > "Yes, you can create as many objects as needed from the same class — that's the whole point of OOP reusability.
5-Year Experience Answer: > "__enter__ runs when entering a with block, __exit__ runs when leaving — whether normally or due to an exception. __exit__ receives exception…
5-Year Experience Answer: > "Class variables are defined at class level and shared across ALL instances — they live in the class's __dict__.
5-Year Experience Answer: > "A stored attribute holds a value in memory.
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Experience Answer: "A stored attribute holds a value in memory. A computed property calculates its value on every access (or uses caching). Example: user.full_name computed from first_name + ' ' + last_name is a computed property — no separate storage, always consistent.
